invariants: The map is generated from one commit by Body Slam. It is never edited by hand; a new commit means a new run.
A family is a package name without its version; its newest version is chosen by version order (0.10 after 0.9, a release after its own -dev builds, dev29 after dev3), not by text order.
A family article quotes only its README and counts from the source; anything else is not claimed.
An older version of a family is not the one to build on unless a family article or its README says why.
procedure: Before using a package, look up its family (corpus estate-index, or the article estate.family.<family>) and take the newest version it names.
To search: rexx bin/bodyslam.rex find DB WORD (family names, README text and public class names).

For classes and methods inside one package, baseline it in Semantic Source Control (osc baseline PATH --repo REPO --component NAME --level 1) and use osc surface and osc source, rather than reading files.
For what breaks if something changes: rexx bin/bodyslam.rex blast DB TARGET.
summary: The estate map holds 515 families of animatedads/alchemy at dd562a52, generated by Body Slam. Use it to find what exists and which version is newest before building anything; read code only after the map has pointed at it.
title: How to use the estate map
